text: Welcome to the consultation. I am Dr. Agent; since the patient is a neonate presenting with seizures and lethargy three days after birth, I need to clarify the delivery history and feeding details. Did the mother have any infections, and are you currently breastfeeding or using formula?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) with secondary seizures.

The history of chorioamnionitis, low Apgar scores, and poor response to resuscitation in a 31-week infant strongly points to perinatal asphyxia. Given the clinical picture, I need to confirm metabolic derangements and rule out sepsis. REQUEST TEST: CBC, Blood Culture, CRP, Blood Glucose, and Electrolytes. REQUEST IMAGES: Head_Ultrasound and EEG.
